definition: Historically, lucidity referred in mental illness to a temporary return of clear thinking and normal understanding, as in a lucid interval when delusions and disordered habits of thought are absent. The term was also used for an alleged ability to perceive beyond the ordinary senses, similar to clairvoyance.
